To address these problems, DroneOps Intelligence is proposed as an integrated software platform for UAV mission planning, monitoring, and incident analytics. The platform focuses on the software layer surrounding UAV operations rather than the development of low-level flight-control algorithms. It provides centralized management of UAVs, operators, missions, waypoints, reviewed mission updates, and flight histories.
The platform supports pre-flight Geofencing and Flight Path Validation to automatically check planned routes against configured No-Fly Zones, restricted areas, and altitude constraints before a mission is approved. During mission execution, standardized UAV telemetry based on MAVLink is delivered to platform services through technologies such as WebSocket or MQTT, allowing operators to monitor the UAV and mission status in real time and detect abnormal operational events.
In addition, DroneOps Intelligence integrates a configured external AI API to summarize supplied mission context, identify potential risks and suggest precautions. Operators and managers review the advice alongside the source mission data; API failures do not block manual review. Therefore, DroneOps Intelligence aims to provide a unified operational environment covering the UAV mission lifecycle from mission planning → pre-flight validation → approval → real-time monitoring → incident detection → post-flight analysis → AI-assisted decision support. By integrating these activities into a single platform, the project aims to improve mission traceability, operational safety, monitoring efficiency, and the effective use of historical UAV mission data.

4. Business OpportunityThe growing use of UAVs creates a need for more efficient and centralized mission-operation management. Existing Ground Control Station systems provide strong capabilities for flight planning, vehicle configuration, and real-time monitoring. However, UAV operations also require effective management of mission records, safety validation, incident histories, and historical flight data to support operational decisions.DroneOps Intelligence addresses this opportunity by providing an integrated platform for mission planning, pre-flight validation, real-time monitoring, incident management, and post-flight analysis. The system validates planned routes against geofences, No-Fly Zones, restricted areas, and altitude limits, while using standardized MAVLink telemetry to monitor UAV operations in real time.A key value of the proposed platform is its ability to consolidate mission information and provide AI-assisted operational insights. By integrating an external AI API, the platform can summarize available mission data and suggest potential risks and precautions for operators and managers to review. This supports mission assessment while keeping the project focused on software integration and operational workflows.Rather than replacing existing flight-control or Ground Control Station software, DroneOps Intelligence focuses on the mission-operation and decision-support layer. By integrating mission validation, telemetry monitoring, incident analytics, and AI-assisted mission assessment into one platform, the system has the potential to improve operational safety, traceability, monitoring efficiency, and data-driven decision-making in UAV operations.

DroneOps Intelligence focuses on providing a software platform for managing UAV mission operations, including mission planning, pre-flight validation, real-time monitoring, incident management, and AI-assisted decision support. The system integrates with MAVLink-compatible UAVs or simulators to receive telemetry data but does not develop or replace low-level flight-control or autopilot algorithms.

AI-generated summaries and recommendations support operators and managers in reviewing missions. They may be incomplete or inaccurate and must be reviewed against the available mission data. The AI component does not autonomously approve, reject, or control UAV missions.
DroneOps Intelligence does not autonomously execute UAV flights. Actual flight execution and vehicle control remain the responsibility of compatible UAV autopilot or Ground Control Station systems.

The entity relationship diagrams describe the mission planning and operational data model. A mission stores the current plan; a separate update request stores proposed changes pending Manager review. Validation, decisions, telemetry, incidents and reports retain their relationship to the relevant mission.

A new mission begins in Draft. Initial submission triggers validation and Manager review. Every subsequent accepted pre-flight edit creates a pending update for the same mission and automatically triggers validation and review. The current mission remains unchanged while review is pending. The lifecycle and concurrency rules are defined in BR-13 and CR-05.
Figure 14. Pending update request lifecycle.

Approval atomically applies proposed content to the same mission ID. Rejecting an update preserves current content and operational status, including an existing Approved status. A mission with a pending update cannot begin execution. Cancellation affects the planning record and never sends a flight-control command.

The entity relationship diagrams describe the mission planning and operational data model. A mission stores the current plan; a separate update request stores proposed changes pending Manager review. Validation, decisions, telemetry, incidents and reports retain their relationship to the relevant mission.

A new mission begins in Draft. Initial submission triggers validation and Manager review. Every subsequent accepted pre-flight edit creates a pending update for the same mission and automatically triggers validation and review. The current mission remains unchanged while review is pending. The lifecycle and concurrency rules are defined in BR-13 and CR-05.
Figure 14. Pending update request lifecycle.

Approval atomically applies proposed content to the same mission ID. Rejecting an update preserves current content and operational status, including an existing Approved status. A mission with a pending update cannot begin execution. Cancellation affects the planning record and never sends a flight-control command.
